business_summary.text: Iris Clothings is an Indian kidswear company transitioning from B2B manufacturing to a D2C brand model under the 'Doreme' brand, with a strategic licensing partnership with Disney.

call_points.text: Planned ₹50 Cr greenfield facility of 200,000 sq. ft. in West Bengal.
Aims for 20,000+ retail touchpoints and 3M+ direct consumers by 2030.
Disney license allows for premium pricing and higher profit margins.
Current manufacturing capacity utilization stands at 75%.
Expanding product portfolio into travel wear, cord sets, and denim pants.
Management expects 30% to 35% revenue growth in FY27.
Digital platforms are expected to contribute ~10% of revenue this year and 20-25% next year.
Planning to add 8 to 10 EBO stores in the coming year.
Vision 2030 targets 300+ distributors, 300+ EBOs, and 20,000+ retail touchpoints across India.
Planning a 200,000 sq. ft. greenfield manufacturing facility in West Bengal with an estimated ₹50 Cr outlay.
Scaling EBOs under the COCO model to ~80 stores before opening FOCO franchise stores post-FY26.

operating_notes.text: Assessed nil financial impact from the New Labour Codes notified in November 2025.

EBO capex is ₹2,500 to ₹3,000 per sq. ft. for a 1,000 sq. ft. store with a payback period of 18-20 months.
D2C platform target customer acquisition cost is ₹250 to ₹300 against average bill value of ₹1,500 to ₹1,600.
In process to acquire 51% stake in Infinia Lifestyle Private Limited for ₹57.12 Cr (₹32.12 Cr equity and ₹25.00 Cr cash).

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹60.48 Cr (+50.4% YoY), net profit ₹6.43 Cr (+43.5% YoY).
Iris Clothings presented Vision 2030 targets and outlined plans for a ₹50 Cr greenfield manufacturing plant in West Bengal.
Iris Clothings presented its Vision 2030 strategy targeting 300+ EBOs and details of a ₹50 Cr greenfield expansion in West Bengal.
Iris Clothings hosted its Q4FY26 earnings call, guiding for 30-35% revenue growth in FY27 and outlining a target of ₹500 Cr revenue from its planned greenfield expansion.
Santosh Ladha, on behalf of Iris Clothings Limited’s promoters and PAC, declared no encumbrances on equity shares for FY2026 under SEBI’s takeover rules (6 April 2026).
Iris Clothings reported Q2FY27 standalone PAT of ₹5.08 Cr on revenue of ₹62.16 Cr and announced progress on acquiring 51% of Infinia Lifestyle for ₹57.12 Cr.
Iris Clothings announced a Vision 2030 plan including a ₹50 Cr greenfield expansion and a target of 300+ EBOs.
